item.title: Spherically Supported Sets with Variable Radii
item.description: arXiv:2610.28789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study closed sets for which, at every boundary point, there exists a containing supporting ball whose prescribed radius may vary from point to point. This extends the notion of spherical support from constant to variable radii. The variable-radius setting presents a new difficulty: unlike the constant-radius case, the intersection of the supporting balls need not be strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii. We overcome this difficulty by associating with every such set a canonical set and an induced radius function determined by the active supporting balls. For continuous prescribed radii, our main result establishes a geometric dichotomy: the original set either coincides with the canonical set and is strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii, or it is contained in the boundary of the canonical set, which is strongly convex with respect to the induced radii. An example shows that the induced radii cannot, in general, be replaced by the prescribed ones in the second alternative. We also recover the constant-radius theory and characterize variable-radius strong convexity in terms of the spherical support of the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Chadi Nour

item.title: A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.28828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.
item.dc:creator: Vsevolod Voronov

item.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.29238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, we show that the existence of such a density $f$ characterizes the assumption on $\Gamma$ up to a constant. There are a few consequences of the above. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \min_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \|x-\lambda\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_G\, \|G\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,I)$. This implies an $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. Second, we establish as a consequence an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem with an explicit constant.
item.dc:creator: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss

item.title: Lipschitz numbers and fine differentiability on metric measure spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a metric space equipped with a doubling measure supporting a Poincar\'e inequality, we introduce capacity-relaxed infinitesimal Lipschitz numbers and characterize Newtonian functions in $N^{1,p}$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and functions of bounded variation. If $X$ is additionally $Q$-regular, then every BV function is $1$-finely differentiable at $\mu$-almost every point, and its fine differential agrees with its approximate Cheeger differential. We also extend a Sobolev regularity criterion from continuous to $p$-quasicontinuous functions.
item.dc:creator: Panu Lahti, Yuxin Li

item.title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2\pi$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11\pi^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Roger Z\"ust

item.title: Macroscopic Poincar\'e Inequalities and Weak-Type Characterizations of $p$-Energy Forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.29789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a class of regular strongly local $p$-energy forms on complete doubling metric measure spaces, $1<p<\infty$, we derive a macroscopic Poincar\'e inequality from a Poincar\'e inequality and a capacity upper bound at a doubling scale $\Psi$. The macroscopic inequality compares $L^p$-oscillations at any two scales and yields a uniform two-scale comparison $J_s\lesssim J_r$, $0<r<s$, for the Korevaar-Schoen functionals, strengthening their usual weak monotonicity property. Conversely, under a density assumption on compactly supported functions, the macroscopic inequality yields a regular strongly local Korevaar-Schoen $p$-energy satisfying a $\Psi$-Poincar\'e inequality. We also show that the macroscopic inequality forces lower $p$-scaling of $\Psi$ on scales not exceeding $\mathrm{diam} X$; together with doubling, this gives two-sided power bounds. Finally, we establish a weak-type characterization of the energy domain of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung type.
item.dc:creator: Fabrice Baudoin, Andrea Pinamonti, Meng Yang

item.title: Solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ in $\lambda$-Cantor sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.29793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ with both coordinates in a $\lambda$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $\alpha>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. To explore the structure of the solutions, for arbitrary $\alpha$, we find that their Hausdorff dimension undergoes phase transitions as $\lambda$ varies: we establish the occurrence of Hausdorff phase transitions by proving the existence of zero-dimensional and positive-dimensional regions.
item.dc:creator: Kan Jiang, Nero Ziyu Li, Lifeng Xi

item.title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.30058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
item.description: arXiv:2607.23453v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson, Grigore Ro\c{s}u

item.title: Poincar\'e Beta Balls: Radial Laws, Hyperbolic Shell Metric Transforms, and Critical-Limit Regimes
item.description: arXiv:2607.26979v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On a high-dimensional Poincar\'e ball, a Euclidean beta-type radial measure concentrates near a sphere, but hyperbolic distance amplifies the surviving radial spread, so the usual shell reduction loses part of the limiting metric. In each regime of the balance between this radial width and amplified angular separation, we determine the weak pyramid limit of the spaces rescaled at the order at which the transition between concentration and dissipation occurs. The four critical-limit regimes are the shifted-exponential railway pyramid, the diameter-at-most-one regime, the nonlinear Gaussian-transform regime, and the Gaussian regime. Each finite-branch railway mm-space generating the first pyramid has branches from a common center, a shifted exponential distribution along them, and paths between different branches through the center. We also give a sharp criterion for convergence to the diameter-at-most-one pyramid. The resulting classification identifies the precise critical scales and clarifies when angular and radial fluctuations contribute simultaneously to the limiting geometry.
item.dc:creator: Shigeaki Yokota

item.title: Union of Translates of a Convex Body
item.description: arXiv:2610.25841v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a strictly convex body and let $Z\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of sites in general position. We consider the problem of calculating the volume $\mu_d$ of $\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K)$. Let $V_z$ be the Voronoi cell of $z\in Z$ with respect to the convex distance function induced by $K$, and let $N$ be the nerve of the Voronoi cells. When $K$ is a ball, a classical result reduces the inclusion-exclusion formula to a sum over $N$: $\mu_d(\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K))=\sum_{J\in N}(-1)^{|J|+1}\mu_d(\bigcap_{z\in J}(z-K))$. When may the hypothesis that $K$ is a ball be dropped? We show that for $d\leq 2$ the reduced formula holds for every strictly convex $K$, while for each $d\geq 3$ there is a strictly convex $K$ for which it fails. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\chi_x$ be the Euler characteristic of the subcomplex of $N$ induced by the sites lying in $K+x$. A sufficient condition for the reduced formula to hold is $\chi_x\equiv 1$ on the union. When $d=3$ and $K$ is $C^4$, we show that $\chi_x\equiv 1$ on the union for all $Z$ in general position if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid. The proof relies on the Fubini-Pick affine invariant.
item.dc:creator: Alec Shelley, Daniel Tartakovsky
